135.matn: Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm al-Ḥanẓalī narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, he said: Maʿmar informed us, from Hammām ibn Munabbih: that he heard Abū Huraira say: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “The prayer of one who has broken his purification is not accepted until he performs ablution.” A man from Ḥaḍramawt said: What is ḥadath, O Abū Huraira? He said: Silent or audible passing of wind.
135.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “No prayer is accepted without purification”. The Prophet ﷺ ties acceptance of the prayer to ablution after ḥadath has occurred. The explanation of what ḥadath is is Abū Huraira’s answer to the questioner from Ḥaḍramawt, not a prophetic saying in this entry.

136.matn: Yaḥyā ibn Bukayr narrated to us, he said: al-Layth narrated to us, from Khālid, from Saʿīd ibn Abī Hilāl, from Nuʿaym al-Mujmir, he said: “I went up with Abū Huraira onto the roof of the mosque, and he performed ablution. Then he said: I heard the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say: My community will be called on the Day of Resurrection with shining foreheads and limbs from the traces of ablution. So whoever among you can lengthen his blaze (al-ghurra), let him do so.”
136.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter on the virtue of ablution and those with shining foreheads and limbs. The radiance is traced to the marks of ablution. The encouragement to lengthen the ghurra is in the wording of this report; a closer definition of how far that goes is not added here.

137.matn: ʿAlī narrated to us, he said: Sufyān narrated to us, he said: al-Zuhrī narrated to us, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, from ʿAbbād ibn Tamīm, from his uncle: “that he complained to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, of the man to whom it seems that he finds the thing in the prayer. He said: He should not step away – or: he should not turn aside – until he hears a sound or finds a smell.”
137.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter that one does not repeat ablution out of doubt until certain. Mere imagination does not break the prayer; certainty here comes by hearing or smelling. The uncertainty “step away or turn aside” is preserved. The uncle remains unnamed, as in the wording.

138.matn: ʿAlī ibn ʿAbdallāh narrated to us, he said: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAmr, he said: Kurayb informed me, from Ibn ʿAbbās: “that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, slept until he snored, then prayed. And he sometimes said: He lay down until he snored, then rose and prayed.” Then Sufyān narrated it to us time after time, from ʿAmr, from Kurayb, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I spent the night at my aunt Maymūna’s. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, rose in the night. When part of the night had passed, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, rose, performed a light ablution from a hanging water-skin – ʿAmr used to describe it as light and little – and stood to pray. I performed an ablution similar to his, then came and stood at his left – and Sufyān sometimes said: at his north side – so he turned me and put me at his right. Then he prayed as long as Allah willed, then lay down and slept until he snored. Then the caller came and announced the prayer to him. He rose with him to the prayer, prayed, and did not perform (a fresh) ablution. We said to ʿAmr: People say: The eye of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sleeps, and his heart does not sleep. ʿAmr said: I heard ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr say: The dreams of the prophets are revelation. Then he recited: “I see in a dream that I am sacrificing you.”
138.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: The same chapter of doubt and certainty in ablution. The report shows that the Prophet ﷺ slept until he snored and then prayed without a fresh ablution. The uncertainties “slept or lay down” and “left or north side” are preserved, as is ʿAmr’s description of the light ablution. The remark that the prophets’ hearts do not sleep stands as a saying “of the people”; ʿAmr supports it with ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr’s word that the prophets’ dreams are revelation, and with the well-known verse. That is marked as a scholar’s note, not a prophetic saying in this chain.

139.matn: ʿAbdallāh ibn Maslama narrated to us, from Mālik, from Mūsā ibn ʿUqba, from Kurayb, the client of Ibn ʿAbbās, from Usāma ibn Zayd: that he heard him say: “The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, moved on from ʿArafa until, when he was at the mountain pass, he dismounted and urinated, then performed ablution and did not do it thoroughly. I said: The prayer, O Messenger of Allah. He said: The prayer is ahead of you. Then he mounted; when he came to al-Muzdalifa he dismounted, performed ablution and did it thoroughly. Then the prayer was established, he prayed the sunset prayer, then each man made his camel kneel at his stopping place, then the night prayer was established and he prayed, and he prayed nothing between them.”
139.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Performing ablution thoroughly”. At the pass he performs an ablution that is not thorough; the prayer is “ahead of you”, at al-Muzdalifa. There he performs it thoroughly and joins the sunset and night prayers with no prayer between them. The difference between the two ablutions is in the text itself.

140.matn: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥīm narrated to us, he said: Abū Salama al-Khuzāʿī Manṣūr ibn Salama informed us, he said: Ibn Bilāl, meaning Sulaymān, informed us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār, from Ibn ʿAbbās: “that he performed ablution and washed his face: he took a handful of water and with it rinsed his mouth and drew water into his nose, then took a handful of water and did like this with it, adding it to his other hand, and washed his face with both, then took a handful of water and washed his right hand with it, then took a handful of water and washed his left hand with it, then wiped his head, then took a handful of water and poured it over his right foot until he had washed it, then took another handful and washed his foot with it, meaning the left. Then he said: Thus I saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, perform ablution.”
140.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Washing the face with both hands from a single handful”. Ibn ʿAbbās demonstrates the ablution. Rinsing the mouth and the nose is from one handful; the face is washed with both hands from a handful added to the other. The gloss “meaning the left” is an explanation by the narrator.

141.matn: ʿAlī ibn ʿAbdallāh narrated to us, he said: Jarīr narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Sālim ibn Abī al-Jaʿd, from Kurayb, from Ibn ʿAbbās, raising it to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, he said: “If one of you, when he comes to his wife, were to say: In the name of Allah, O Allah, keep Satan away from us and keep Satan away from what You have provided us, and then a child were decreed between them, it would not harm him.”
141.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Saying Allah’s name in every state and at intercourse”. The formula is at the start of intercourse; the protection concerns the child, if one is granted. The wording does not specify the harm more closely, and that is not supplied here.

142.matn: Ādam narrated to us, he said: Shuʿba narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Ṣuhayb, he said: I heard Anas say: “When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, entered the toilet, he said: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from foulness and the foul ones (al-khubuth wa-l-khabāʾith).” Ibn ʿArʿara corroborated him (in narrating) from Shuʿba. Ghundar said, from Shuʿba: when he came to the toilet. Mūsā said, from Ḥammād: when he entered. Saʿīd ibn Zayd said: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz narrated to us: when he wanted to enter.
142.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “What to say on entering the toilet”. The plea for refuge is constant; the wordings “entered, came, went in, wanted to enter” are preserved as narrator variants. Ibn ʿArʿara’s following is marked as a supporting path.

143.matn: ʿAbdallāh ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, he said: Hāshim ibn al-Qāsim narrated to us, he said: Warqāʾ narrated to us, from ʿUbaydallāh ibn Abī Yazīd, from Ibn ʿAbbās: “that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, entered the toilet, and I placed water for ablution for him. He said: Who put this here? He was told. Then he said: O Allah, grant him understanding in the religion.”
143.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Placing water at the toilet”. Ibn ʿAbbās sets out the water; the supplication for understanding in the religion is for him. Who gave the report remains unnamed in the wording.

144.matn: Ādam narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abī Dhiʾb narrated to us, he said: al-Zuhrī narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yazīd al-Laythī, from Abū Ayyūb al-Anṣārī, he said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “When one of you comes to relieve himself, let him not face the qibla nor turn his back to it; face east or west.”
144.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter on not facing the qibla when relieving oneself, except in a building. The instruction “east or west” fits the situation of Medina, where the qibla is to the south; an extension to other bearings is not fixed here. The chapter itself names the exception behind a wall; this entry does not spell it out.

145.matn: ʿAbdallāh ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, he said: Mālik informed us, from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā ibn Ḥibbān, from his uncle Wāsiʿ ibn Ḥibbān, from ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿUmar: “that he used to say: People say: When you sit for your need, do not face the qibla or the Sacred House (Bayt al-Maqdis). ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿUmar said: I went up one day onto the roof of a house of ours and saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, on two bricks, facing the Sacred House, for his need. And he said: Perhaps you are of those who pray on their hips? I said: I do not know, by Allah.” Mālik said: He means the one who prays and does not rise from the ground, who prostrates while stuck to the earth.
145.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “One who relieved himself squatting on two bricks”. Ibn ʿUmar counters the general claim with what he himself saw: the Prophet ﷺ with his back to the qibla and his face toward the Sacred House, in a built area. The question about “praying on the hips” is Ibn ʿUmar’s address to his interlocutor, not a prophetic saying. Mālik’s explanation of that posture is marked as a scholar’s note.

146.matn: Yaḥyā ibn Bukayr narrated to us, he said: al-Layth narrated to us, he said: ʿUqayl narrated to me, from Ibn Shihāb, from ʿUrwa, from ʿĀʾisha: “that the wives of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to go out at night, when they relieved themselves, to the manāṣiʿ, which is an open, spacious tract of ground. ʿUmar used to say to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: Veil your women. But the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would not do so. Then Sawda bint Zamʿa, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went out one night in the evening. She was a tall woman, so ʿUmar called out to her: We have recognized you, O Sawda! — out of eagerness that the ḥijāb be sent down. So Allah sent down the verse of the ḥijāb.”
146.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Women going out to relieve themselves”. The wives went out at night to the manāṣiʿ; the phrase “an open, spacious tract of ground” explains that place. ʿUmar asked that they be veiled; the Messenger of Allah did not yet do so. The call to tall Sawda was, as the wording records, from a desire that the ḥijāb be sent down; Allah then sent down the verse of the ḥijāb. Which verses are meant is not fixed in this entry.

147.matn: Zakariyyāʾ narrated to us, he said: Abū Usāma narrated to us, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwa, from his father, from ʿĀʾisha, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, he said: “You have been permitted to go out for your need.” Hishām said: meaning relieving oneself (al-barāz).
147.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter “Women going out to relieve themselves”. The permission is to go out “for your need”. The gloss “meaning relieving oneself” is Hishām’s explanation and remains marked as a narrator’s note.

148.matn: Ibrāhīm ibn al-Mundhir narrated to us, he said: Anas ibn ʿIyāḍ narrated to us, from ʿUbayd Allāh, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā ibn Ḥibbān, from Wāsiʿ ibn Ḥibbān, from ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿUmar, he said: “I climbed onto the roof of Ḥafṣa’s house for some need of mine, and I saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, relieving himself with his back to the qibla, facing al-Shām.”
148.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Relieving oneself in houses”. Ibn ʿUmar sees the Messenger of Allah on the roof of Ḥafṣa’s house: his back to the qibla, his face toward al-Shām. That this is in a built area matches the chapter heading; differences among the schools over open ground and built space are not settled here.

149.matn: Yaʿqūb ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to us, he said: Yazīd ibn Hārūn narrated to us, he said: Yaḥyā informed us, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā ibn Ḥibbān, that his uncle Wāsiʿ ibn Ḥibbān informed him: that ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿUmar informed him, he said: “I went up one day onto the roof of our house, and I saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sitting on two bricks, facing the Sacred House (Bayt al-Maqdis).”
149.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: This entry has no chapter title in the corpus; none is added here. The report is close to the previous one and to that of the two bricks: Ibn ʿUmar sees the Messenger of Allah on the roof of “our house”, on two bricks, facing the Sacred House.

150.matn: Abū al-Walīd Hishām ibn ʿAbd al-Malik narrated to us, he said: Shuʿba narrated to us, from Abū Muʿādh, whose name is ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Maymūna, he said: I heard Anas ibn Mālik say: “When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went out for his need, I and a boy would come, we had with us a vessel of water (idāwa),” meaning he would cleanse himself with it.
150.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Cleaning oneself with water after relieving oneself”. Anas and a boy bring a water-vessel. The gloss “meaning he would cleanse himself with it” is a narrator’s explanation. Abū Muʿādh is identified as ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Maymūna. Other ways of cleaning, such as with stones, are not treated in this wording.

151.matn: Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb narrated to us, he said: Shuʿba narrated to us, from Abū Muʿādh, that is ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Maymūna, he said: I heard Anas say: “When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went out for his need, I and a boy from among us followed him, we had with us a vessel of water (idāwa).”
151.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “One who carries water with him for purification”. The report is like the previous one; here it says that Anas and a boy from among us followed him with a water-vessel. The gloss about cleaning with water is not in this wording. The identification “that is ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Maymūna” is a narrator’s note.

152.matn: Muḥammad ibn Bashshār narrated to us, he said: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, he said: Shuʿba narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Maymūna: he heard Anas ibn Mālik say: “The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to enter the privy, and I and a boy would carry a vessel of water (idāwa) and a short spear (ʿanaza); he would cleanse himself with the water.” Al-Naḍr and Shādhān followed him (in the narration) from Shuʿba. The ʿanaza: a staff with a spear-tip (zujj).
152.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Carrying a short spear (ʿanaza) along with water for cleaning”. Anas and a boy carry a water-vessel and an ʿanaza; the cleaning is with water. The follow-up of al-Naḍr and Shādhān is marked as a supporting path. The gloss of the ʿanaza as a staff with a tip is a lexical note; the purpose of the staff is not stated in this wording.

153.matn: Muʿādh ibn Faḍāla narrated to us, he said: Hishām narrated to us, that is al-Dastuwāʾī, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, from ʿAbdallāh ibn Abī Qatāda, from his father, he said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “When one of you drinks, let him not breathe into the vessel; and when he comes to the privy, let him not touch his private part with his right hand, nor clean himself with his right hand.”
153.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The prohibition of cleaning oneself with the right hand”. The wording joins three instructions: not breathing into the vessel, not touching the private part with the right hand, and not cleaning oneself with the right hand. The identification “that is al-Dastuwāʾī” is a narrator’s note. Whether the prohibition is strict or a matter of disapproval is not decided in this entry.

154.matn: Muḥammad ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, he said: al-Awzāʿī narrated to us, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, from ʿAbdallāh ibn Abī Qatāda, from his father, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, he said: “When one of you urinates, let him not take his private part with his right hand, nor cleanse himself with his right hand, nor breathe into the vessel.”
154.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Not holding one’s private part with the right hand while urinating”. The same matter appears in another order and with the verbs “take” and “cleanse (istinjāʾ)” rather than “touch” and “wipe”. The three instructions remain in the wording; no ranking of the formulations is fixed here.

155.matn: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad al-Makkī narrated to us, he said: ʿAmr ibn Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd ibn ʿAmr al-Makkī narrated to us, from his grandfather, from Abū Huraira, he said: “I followed the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, as he went out for his need. He would not look around. I drew near to him and he said: Seek stones for me, I will cleanse myself with them, or the like, and do not bring me a bone or dung. So I brought him stones in the edge of my garment, placed them at his side and turned away from him. When he had finished, he followed it with them.”
155.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Cleaning oneself with stones”. The Prophet ﷺ asks for stones for cleaning and excludes bone and dung; the reason is not stated in this wording. The phrase “or the like” preserves a narrator’s uncertainty. Abū Huraira lays the stones aside and turns away; after finishing they are used.

156.matn: Abū Nuʿaym narrated to us, he said: Zuhayr narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, he said: It was not Abū ʿUbayda who mentioned it, but ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Aswad, from his father: that he heard ʿAbdallāh say: “The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came to the place of relieving himself and ordered me to bring him three stones. I found two stones and sought the third but did not find it, so I took a piece of dung and brought it to him. He took the two stones and threw away the dung and said: This is rikz (filth).”
156.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter “Cleaning oneself with stones”. Abū Isḥāq corrects the isnād: the mention was not from Abū ʿUbayda, but from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Aswad from his father; ʿAbdallāh in this well-known report is Ibn Masʿūd. Three stones are asked for; two are accepted, the dung is rejected as rikz. Whether three stones are required is not decided in this entry.

157.matn: Muḥammad ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, he said: Sufyān narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: “The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, performed ablution washing each part once.”
157.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Ablution washing each part once”. Ibn ʿAbbās attests to washing the limbs once each. Other numbers, such as twice or three times, are not treated in this wording; they appear in the following chapters.

158.matn: Ḥusayn ibn ʿĪsā narrated to us, he said: Yūnus ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, he said: Fulayḥ ibn Sulaymān narrated to us, from ʿAbdallāh ibn Abī Bakr ibn ʿAmr ibn Ḥazm, from ʿAbbād ibn Tamīm, from ʿAbdallāh ibn Zayd: “that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, performed ablution washing each part twice.”
158.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Ablution washing each part twice”. ʿAbdallāh ibn Zayd attests to washing twice. Other numbers are not treated in this wording; washing once is in the previous chapter, three times in the next.

159.matn: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn ʿAbdallāh al-Uwaysī narrated to us, he said: Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd narrated to me, from Ibn Shihāb: that ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yazīd informed him: that Ḥumrān, the mawlā of ʿUthmān, informed him: “that he saw ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān call for a vessel, pour it over his palms three times and wash them, then put his right hand into the vessel, rinse his mouth and draw water into his nose, then wash his face three times, and his arms up to the elbows three times, then wipe his head, then wash his feet three times up to the ankles, then said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever performs ablution like this ablution of mine, then prays two rakʿas without talking to himself in them, will be forgiven what has preceded of his sin.”
159.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Ablution washing each part three times”. Ḥumrān describes ʿUthmān’s ablution: the palms three times, the face, arms and feet three times; mouth, nose and the wiping of the head are without a number. The promise is for an ablution “like this” and two rakʿas without self-converse. The scope of the forgiveness is not fixed more closely in this wording.

160.matn: And from Ibrāhīm, he said: Ṣāliḥ ibn Kaysān said: Ibn Shihāb said: But ʿUrwa narrates from Ḥumrān: “When ʿUthmān had performed ablution, he said: Shall I not tell you a hadith? Were it not for a verse, I would not have told it to you. I heard the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say: A man does not perform ablution, doing it well, and pray the prayer, but that he is forgiven what is between him and the prayer until he prays it.” ʿUrwa said: The verse: “Those who conceal what We have sent down of clear proofs.”
160.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter. The path comes from Ibrāhīm; Ibn Shihāb sets ʿUrwa’s narration from Ḥumrān against the previous one. ʿUthmān ties the telling to a verse; ʿUrwa’s identification of the verse (the opening of al-Baqara 2:159) is marked as a scholar’s note. The wording of the verse is not completed beyond the quotation.

161.matn: ʿAbdān narrated to us, he said: ʿAbdallāh informed us, he said: Yūnus informed us, from al-Zuhrī, he said: Abū Idrīs informed me that he heard Abū Huraira, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “Whoever performs ablution, let him blow his nose; and whoever cleans himself with stones, let him do so an odd number of times.”
161.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Blowing out the nose in ablution”. Two instructions stand together: expelling the water from the nose, and an odd number when cleaning with stones. A closer ruling of obligation is not fixed here.

162.matn: ʿAbdallāh ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, he said: Mālik informed us, from Abū al-Zinād, from al-Aʿraj, from Abū Huraira: that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “When one of you performs ablution, let him put (water) into his nose then blow it out; and whoever cleans himself with stones, let him do so an odd number of times; and when one of you wakes from his sleep, let him wash his hand before putting it into his ablution water, for one of you does not know where his hand has spent the night.”
162.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Using stones an odd number of times”. The wording joins putting water in the nose and blowing it out, the odd number, and washing the hand after sleep before dipping it into the ablution water. The reason remains the uncertainty of where the hand spent the night; a further interpretation and the question of obligation are not decided here.

163.matn: Mūsā narrated to us, he said: Abū ʿAwāna narrated to us, from Abū Bishr, from Yūsuf ibn Māhak, from ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿAmr, he said: “The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, lagged behind us on a journey we made, then he caught up with us when ʿaṣr had already pressed us. We began to perform ablution and wipe over our feet. He called out at the top of his voice: Woe to the heels from the Fire. Twice or three times.”
163.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Washing the feet, not merely wiping over them”. The warning concerns the heels, while they were wiping over the feet. “Twice or three times” remains as a narrator’s uncertainty. The chapter heading points to washing rather than mere wiping; differences of opinion on that are not settled here.

164.matn: Abū al-Yamān narrated to us, he said: Shuʿayb informed us, from al-Zuhrī, he said: ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yazīd informed me, from Ḥumrān, the mawlā of ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān: “that he saw ʿUthmān call for ablution water, pour from his vessel over his hands and wash them three times, then put his right hand into the ablution water, then rinse his mouth, draw water into his nose and blow it out, then wash his face three times, and his arms up to the elbows three times, then wipe his head, then wash each foot three times, then said: I saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, perform ablution like this ablution of mine, and he said: Whoever performs ablution like this ablution of mine, then prays two rakʿas without talking to himself in them, Allah will forgive him what has preceded of his sin.”
164.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Rinsing the mouth in ablution”. The account is close to the previous report of ʿUthmān’s ablution; here rinsing the mouth, drawing in and blowing out are stated expressly, and “each foot” is washed three times, without mention of the ankles. Mouth, nose and the wiping of the head remain without a number. The promise is for an ablution “like this” and two rakʿas without self-converse.

165.matn: Ādam ibn Abī Iyās narrated to us, he said: Shuʿba narrated to us, he said: Muḥammad ibn Ziyād narrated to us, he said: “I heard Abū Huraira — and he used to pass by us while the people were performing ablution from the purification vessel (maṭhara) — he said: Perform the ablution thoroughly, for Abū al-Qāsim, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: Woe to the heels from the Fire.”
165.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Washing the heels”. Abū Huraira urges a thorough ablution and rests it on the word of Abū al-Qāsim ﷺ about the heels. The scene at the purification vessel is a description by the narrator Muḥammad ibn Ziyād.

166.matn: ʿAbdallāh ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, he said: Mālik informed us, from Saʿīd al-Maqburī, from ʿUbayd ibn Jurayj, that he said to ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿUmar: “O Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, I have seen you do four things that I have not seen any of your companions do. He said: And what are they, O Ibn Jurayj? He said: I have seen you touch of the corners only the two Yemeni ones, I have seen you wear the sibtiyya sandals, I have seen you dye with yellow, and I have seen that when you were in Mecca the people made the ihlāl when they saw the new moon, while you did not until it was the day of Tarwiyah. ʿAbdallāh said: As for the corners: I did not see the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, touch any but the two Yemeni ones. As for the sibtiyya sandals: I saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, wear the sandal that has no hair in it and perform ablution in it, so I like to wear them. As for the yellow: I saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, dye with it, so I like to dye with it. As for the ihlāl: I did not see the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, make the ihlāl until his mount set out with him.”
166.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Washing the feet in sandals, not wiping over the sandals”. Of the four practices, the one that bears on the chapter is performing ablution in the hairless sandal; the wording says “in it”, not wiping over the sandal. The other three points — the two Yemeni corners, dyeing with yellow, and the ihlāl only when the mount sets out, not already at the new moon — remain in the report, without this entry settling the questions of ḥajj or dyeing.

167.matn: Musaddad narrated to us, he said: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: Khālid narrated to us, from Ḥafṣa bint Sīrīn, from Umm ʿAṭiyya, she said: “The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to them, regarding the washing of his daughter: Begin with her right sides and the places of ablution on her.”
167.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Starting with the right in ablution and bathing”. The instruction is to the women at the funeral washing of his daughter: first her right sides and the places of ablution. The daughter’s name is not given in this wording and is not added here.

168.matn: Ḥafṣ ibn ʿUmar narrated to us, he said: Shuʿba narrated to us, he said: Ashʿath ibn Sulaym informed me, he said: I heard my father, from Masrūq, from ʿĀʾisha, she said: “The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, liked starting with the right in putting on his sandals, in combing his hair, and in his purification, in all his affairs.”
168.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter. ʿĀʾisha attests the preference for the right in sandals, hair and purification, and adds “in all his affairs”. It is Ashʿath who states that he heard it from his father.

169.matn: ʿAbdallāh ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, he said: Mālik informed us, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAbdallāh ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, from Anas ibn Mālik, that he said: “I saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and the time of the ʿaṣr prayer had come. The people sought ablution water and did not find it. Ablution water was brought to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, put his hand in that vessel and ordered the people to perform ablution from it. He said: I saw the water springing from under his fingers until they had performed ablution, to the last of them.”
169.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Seeking water for ablution when the prayer time comes”. The people seek ablution water and find none; after the hand is placed in the vessel, the water springs from under the fingers until the last of them has performed ablution. This wording does not give a number of those present.

170.matn: Mālik ibn Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim, from Ibn Sīrīn, he said: “I said to ʿAbīda: We have some of the hair of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace; we obtained it from Anas, or from the family of Anas. He said: That I should have a single hair of his would be dearer to me than the world and what is in it.”
170.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The water with which human hair is washed”. Ibn Sīrīn keeps the uncertainty whether the hair came from Anas or from his family. ʿAbīda prefers a single hair of the Prophet to the world and what is in it. This wording gives no further number or origin for the hair.

171.matn: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥīm narrated to us, he said: Saʿīd ibn Sulaymān informed us, he said: ʿAbbād narrated to us, from Ibn ʿAwn, from Ibn Sīrīn, from Anas: “that when the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, shaved his head, Abū Ṭalḥa was the first to take from his hair.”
171.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter. Anas reports that Abū Ṭalḥa was the first to take from the Messenger’s hair when he shaved his head. This wording names no place, occasion, or further recipients.

172.matn: ʿAbdallāh ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, from Mālik, from Abū al-Zinād, from al-Aʿraj, from Abū Huraira, he said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “If the dog drinks from the vessel of one of you, let him wash it seven times.”
172.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter. The wording requires washing seven times a vessel from which a dog has drunk. This version does not mention washing with earth. The text does not decide the legal status of the leftover water.

173.matn: Isḥāq narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad informed us, he said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbdallāh ibn Dīnār narrated to us, he said: I heard my father, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Abū Huraira, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: “that a man saw a dog eating the moist earth from thirst. The man took his khuff and began scooping for it with it, until he quenched its thirst. Allah thanked him for it and admitted him to Paradise.”
173.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter. The source names the transmitter only as Isḥāq, without a further name. A man waters a thirsty dog with his khuff; Allah thanks him and admits him to Paradise. This wording names no well or place.

174.matn: Aḥmad ibn Shabīb said: My father narrated to us, from Yūnus, from Ibn Shihāb, he said: Ḥamza ibn ʿAbdallāh narrated to me, from his father, he said: “The dogs used to urinate and come and go in the mosque in the time of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and they did not sprinkle anything of that.”
174.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī brings this hadith without a complete chain of his own (muʿallaq) with the words “Aḥmad ibn Shabīb said”, under the same chapter. Ḥamza reports from his father that dogs used to urinate and move about in the mosque and that nothing of that was sprinkled. The wording states neither a cleansing act nor a legal conclusion; it does not settle disagreements on the matter.

175.matn: Ḥafṣ ibn ʿUmar narrated to us, he said: Shuʿba narrated to us, from Ibn Abī al-Safar, from al-Shaʿbī, from ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim, he said: “I asked the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and he said: If you send out your trained dog and it kills, then eat; and if it eats, then do not eat, for it has held it only for itself. I said: I send out my dog and find another dog with it? He said: Then do not eat, for you pronounced the name only over your dog, and you did not pronounce it over another dog.”
175.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter. ʿAdī asks about hunting with the trained dog: if it kills and does not itself eat, one may eat; if the dog has eaten of it, one may not eat. If another dog is found with it, one may not eat, because the naming was only over one’s own dog. This wording does not decide further hunting rules.

176.matn: Ādam ibn Abī Iyās narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abī Dhiʾb narrated to us, from Saʿīd al-Maqburī, from Abū Huraira, he said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “The servant remains in prayer as long as he is in the mosque waiting for the prayer, so long as he has not had a ḥadath.” A non-Arab man said: What is ḥadath, O Abū Huraira? He said: The sound; meaning the passing of wind.
176.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “One who holds ablution necessary only for what comes out of the two passages”. Waiting in the mosque counts as prayer so long as no ḥadath occurs. Abū Huraira explains ḥadath here as the sound, meaning the passing of wind. This wording does not extend it to other kinds of ḥadath.

177.matn: Abū al-Walīd narrated to us, he said: Ibn ʿUyayna narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿAbbād ibn Tamīm, from his uncle, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, he said: “He should not leave until he hears a sound or detects a smell.”
177.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter. The uncle is not named in this chain. One is not to leave the prayer until a sound is heard or a smell is detected. The wording does not settle doubt by mere conjecture.

178.matn: Qutayba ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, he said: Jarīr narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Mundhir Abū Yaʿlā al-Thawrī, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥanafiyya, he said: ʿAlī said: “I was a man who frequently had madhy (pre-seminal fluid), and I was ashamed to ask the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, so I told al-Miqdād ibn al-Aswad to ask him, and he said: For it there is ablution.” Shuʿba also narrated it from al-Aʿmash.
178.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter. Out of shyness ʿAlī has al-Miqdād ask; the answer is that madhy requires ablution. This wording does not mention a ritual bath. The closing note records another route through Shuʿba from al-Aʿmash.

179.matn: Saʿd ibn Ḥafṣ narrated to us, Shaybān narrated to us, from Yaḥyā, from Abū Salama: that ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār informed him: that Zayd ibn Khālid informed him: that he asked ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān, may Allah be pleased with him, I said: “What do you say if a man has intercourse and does not ejaculate?” ʿUthmān said: He performs ablution as he performs it for prayer, and he washes his private part. ʿUthmān said: I heard it from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Then I asked about that ʿAlī, al-Zubayr, Ṭalḥa and Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, may Allah be pleased with them, and they instructed him to do that.
179.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter. When there is no ejaculation, ʿUthmān joins ablution and washing the private part to what he heard from the Messenger; ʿAlī, al-Zubayr, Ṭalḥa and Ubayy ibn Kaʿb gave the same instruction. This wording does not decide other reports or later evaluations.

180.matn: Isḥāq narrated to us, he said: al-Naḍr informed us, he said: Shuʿba informed us, from al-Ḥakam, from Dhakwān Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī: “that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sent for a man of the Ansar, and he came with his head dripping. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: Perhaps we have hurried you? He said: Yes. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: If you have been hurried or you have had no emission, then ablution is upon you.” Wahb followed him in this, he said: Shuʿba narrated to us. Abū ʿAbdallāh said: Ghundar and Yaḥyā did not say, from Shuʿba: the ablution.
180.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter. The source names the transmitter only as Isḥāq, without a further name; the man of the Ansar remains unnamed. In the case of haste or no emission, ablution is mentioned. Al-Bukhārī (Abū ʿAbdallāh) notes that Ghundar and Yaḥyā do not transmit from Shuʿba the words “the ablution”; Wahb follows the version that has this word. The transmitters’ divergence is left standing.

181.matn: Muḥammad ibn Salām narrated to me, he said: Yazīd ibn Hārūn informed us, from Yaḥyā, from Mūsā ibn ʿUqba, from Kurayb, the mawlā of Ibn ʿAbbās, from Usāma ibn Zayd: “that when the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, moved on from ʿArafa, he turned aside to the mountain pass and relieved himself. Usāma ibn Zayd said: I began pouring over him while he performed ablution, and I said: O Messenger of Allah, will you pray? He said: The prayer place is ahead of you.”
181.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “A man helping his companion perform ablution”. Usāma pours the water while the Messenger performs ablution in the pass after leaving ʿArafa. The prayer place is said to lie ahead; this wording gives no place-name. No numbers of washings are stated.

182.matn: ʿAmr ibn ʿAlī narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Wahhāb narrated to us, he said: I heard Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, he said: Saʿd ibn Ibrāhīm informed me that Nāfiʿ ibn Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim informed him: that he heard ʿUrwa ibn al-Mughīra ibn Shuʿba narrating from al-Mughīra ibn Shuʿba: “that he was with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, on a journey, and that he went for a need of his, and that al-Mughīra began pouring water over him while he performed ablution. He washed his face and his hands, wiped over his head, and wiped over the khuffs.”
182.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter. Al-Mughīra pours the water; face, hands, wiping the head and wiping over the khuffs are mentioned. This wording gives no numbers and no further detail of the journey.

183.matn: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: Mālik narrated to me, from Makhrama ibn Sulaymān, from Kurayb, the mawlā of Ibn ʿAbbās: that ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿAbbās informed him: “that he spent a night at Maymūna’s, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and she was his maternal aunt. I lay across the width of the cushion, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and his wife lay along its length. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, slept until it was midnight, or a little before, or a little after. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, woke, sat wiping the sleep from his face with his hand, then recited the ten closing verses of Sūrat Āl ʿImrān, then went to a hanging waterskin, performed ablution from it and did his ablution well, then stood and prayed. Ibn ʿAbbās said: I got up and did as he had done, then I went and stood at his side. He placed his right hand on my head and took my right ear and twisted it. He prayed two rakʿas, then two, then two, then two, then two, then two, then he prayed witr, then he lay down until the muezzin came to him. Then he got up and prayed two light rakʿas, then went out and prayed the dawn prayer.”
183.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Reciting the Qurʾān after breaking ablution, and other matters”. The time remains uncertain: midnight, a little before, or a little after. The recitation of the ten closing verses of Āl ʿImrān comes before the described ablution from the hanging waterskin; this wording does not expressly mention a ḥadath and does not decide the legal question. Ibn ʿAbbās copies him and stands at his side; the right ear is twisted. There follow six times two rakʿas, the witr, after the muezzin two light rakʿas, and the dawn prayer.

184.matn: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: Mālik narrated to me, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwa, from his wife Fāṭima, from her grandmother Asmāʾ bint Abī Bakr, that she said: “I came to ʿĀʾisha, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, when the sun was eclipsed. There were the people standing in prayer, and she was standing in prayer. I said: What is the matter with the people? She pointed with her hand toward the sky and said: Subḥān Allāh. I said: A sign? She gestured: yes. I stood until fainting overcame me, and I began pouring water over my head. When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, finished, he praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: There is nothing I had not seen except that I have seen it in this standing of mine, even Paradise and the Fire. And it has been revealed to me that you will be tried in the graves like the trial of the Dajjāl, or close to it — I do not know which of those Asmāʾ said —: one of you will be brought and it will be said: What is your knowledge of this man? As for the believer, or the one with certainty — I do not know which of those Asmāʾ said — he will say: He is Muḥammad, the Messenger of Allah; he came to us with the clear signs and the guidance, so we answered, believed and followed. It will be said: Sleep righteously, for we have known that you were a believer. As for the hypocrite or the doubter — I do not know which of those Asmāʾ said — he will say: I do not know; I heard the people saying something, so I said it.”
184.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “One who renewed ablution only after heavy fainting”. Asmāʾ is overcome by fainting and pours water over her head; this wording does not mention a renewed ablution and does not decide the legal question. Three times the narrator’s uncertainty is kept as to which word Asmāʾ used. The Messenger reports that in his standing he saw Paradise and the Fire, and speaks of the trial in the grave, like that of the Dajjāl or close to it.

185.matn: ʿAbdallāh ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, he said: Mālik informed us, from ʿAmr ibn Yaḥyā al-Māzinī, from his father: “that a man said to ʿAbdallāh ibn Zayd, and he was the grandfather of ʿAmr ibn Yaḥyā: Can you show me how the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, performed ablution? ʿAbdallāh ibn Zayd said: Yes. He called for water, poured over his hands and washed them twice, then rinsed his mouth and blew his nose three times, then washed his face three times, then washed his arms twice each to the elbows, then wiped his head with his hands, bringing them forward and back; he began at the front of his head until he took them to the nape, then returned them to the place from which he had started, then he washed his feet.”
185.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Wiping the whole head”. The wording calls ʿAbdallāh ibn Zayd the grandfather of ʿAmr ibn Yaḥyā. The numbers are: hands twice, mouth and blowing the nose three times, face three times, arms twice each to the elbows; the wiping of the head goes from the front to the nape and back. This version states no number for the feet.

186.matn: Mūsā narrated to us, he said: Wuhayb narrated to us, from ʿAmr, from his father: “I was present when ʿAmr ibn Abī Ḥasan asked ʿAbdallāh ibn Zayd about the ablution of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He called for a vessel (tawr) of water and performed for them the ablution of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He poured from the vessel over his hand and washed his hands three times, then put his hand into the vessel, rinsed his mouth, drew water into the nose and blew it out, in three handfuls, then put his hand in and washed his face three times, then washed his arms twice to the elbows, then put his hand in and wiped his head, bringing them forward and back, once, then washed his feet to the ankles.”
186.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Washing the feet up to the ankles”. ʿAmr’s father witnesses the question of ʿAmr ibn Abī Ḥasan. The numbers are: hands three times, mouth, nose and blowing out in three handfuls, face three times, arms twice to the elbows, wiping the head once forward and back. The feet are washed to the ankles; this version states no number for them.

187.matn: Ādam narrated to us, he said: Shuʿba narrated to us, he said: al-Ḥakam narrated to us, he said: I heard Abū Juḥayfa say: “The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came out to us in the midday heat. Ablution water was brought and he performed ablution. The people began taking from the leftover of his ablution water and wiping themselves with it. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed the ẓuhr prayer in two rakʿas and the ʿaṣr prayer in two rakʿas, and in front of him was a ʿanaza.”
187.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Using the leftover water of people's ablution”. The people take from the leftover water and wipe themselves with it. Ẓuhr and ʿaṣr are each mentioned as two rakʿas; this wording names no occasion of travel. In front of him stands a ʿanaza.

188.matn: Abū Mūsā said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, called for a cup with water in it, washed his hands and his face in it, sprayed (a little water from his mouth) into it, then said to the two of them: Drink from it, and pour it over your faces and your upper chests.
188.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī brings this hadith without a complete chain of his own (muʿallaq) with the words “Abū Mūsā said”, under the same chapter. The Prophet washes hands and face in the vessel, sprays into it, and tells the two to drink from it and pour it over face and upper chest. The two who are addressed remain unnamed.

189.matn: ʿAlī ibn ʿAbdallāh narrated to us, he said: Yaʿqūb ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to us, from Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn Shihāb, he said: “Maḥmūd ibn al-Rabīʿ informed me, he said: And he is the one into whose face the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sprayed (water from his mouth) when he was a boy, from their well.” ʿUrwa said, from al-Miswar and others, each of them confirming his companion: When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, performed ablution, they almost came to blows over his leftover water.
189.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter. The first route names Maḥmūd ibn al-Rabīʿ as the boy into whose face water was sprayed from their well. Al-Bukhārī adds ʿUrwa’s report from al-Miswar and others without a complete chain of his own; each confirms the other that they almost came to blows over the leftover water.

190.matn: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yūnus narrated to us, he said: Ḥātim ibn Ismāʿīl narrated to us, from al-Jaʿd, he said: I heard al-Sāʾib ibn Yazīd say: “My maternal aunt took me to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of Allah, my sister’s son is in pain. He wiped my head and prayed for blessing for me, then performed ablution, and I drank from his leftover water. Then I stood behind his back and looked at the seal of prophethood between his shoulder blades, like the button of a ḥajala.”
190.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter. The maternal aunt remains unnamed. Al-Sāʾib drinks from the leftover water after the Prophet has wiped his head and prayed for blessing. The seal lies between the shoulder blades, “like the button of a ḥajala”; ḥajala is understood either as a bird or as a canopy, and this wording does not decide that.

191.matn: Musaddad narrated to us, he said: Khālid ibn ʿAbdallāh narrated to us, he said: ʿAmr ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, from his father, from ʿAbdallāh ibn Zayd: “that he poured from the vessel over his hands and washed them, then washed — or rinsed his mouth and drew water into the nose — from a single handful, and he did that three times, then washed his arms to the elbows twice each, wiped his head, the front and the back, and washed his feet to the ankles, then said: This was the ablution of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.”
191.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “One who rinsed mouth and nose from a single handful”. The uncertainty “washed, or rinsed the mouth and drew water into the nose” from one handful is kept; that was done three times. The hands at the start have no number; the arms twice each to the elbows; the feet to the ankles with no number. ʿAbdallāh ibn Zayd presents this as the Messenger’s ablution.

192.matn: Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb narrated to us, he said: Wuhayb narrated to us, he said: ʿAmr ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, from his father, he said: “I was present when ʿAmr ibn Abī Ḥasan asked ʿAbdallāh ibn Zayd about the ablution of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He called for a vessel (tawr) of water and performed the ablution for them. He poured over his hands and washed them three times, then put his hand into the vessel, rinsed his mouth, drew water into the nose and blew it out three times, with three handfuls of water, then put his hand into the vessel and washed his face three times, then put his hand into the vessel and washed his arms to the elbows twice each, then put his hand into the vessel and wiped his head, bringing his hands forward and back, then put his hand into the vessel and washed his feet.” And Mūsā narrated to us, he said: Wuhayb narrated to us, he said: He wiped his head once.
192.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Wiping the head once”. The first route describes bringing the hands forward and back over the head without the word “once”. The route of Mūsā from Wuhayb adds: He wiped his head once. The feet are washed with no number and no mention of the ankles.

193.matn: ʿAbdallāh ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, he said: Mālik informed us, from Nāfiʿ, from ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿUmar, that he said: “Men and women used to perform ablution together in the time of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.”
193.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “A man's ablution with his wife, and the woman's leftover water”. The wording says only that men and women performed ablution together in that time. It does not decide whether the same vessel, leftover water, or further legal questions are meant.

194.matn: Abū al-Walīd narrated to us, he said: Shuʿba narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn al-Munkadir, he said: I heard Jābir say: “The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came to visit me while I was ill and not in my senses. He performed ablution and poured over me from his leftover water. Then I came to my senses and said: O Messenger of Allah, to whom is the inheritance? Only kalāla inherits from me. Then the verse of the appointed shares was sent down.”
194.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The Prophet ﷺ pouring his ablution water over one who had fainted”. Jābir is ill and unconscious; after the leftover water is poured over him he recovers and asks about inheritance as kalāla. The wording names “the verse of the appointed shares” without a verse number. Kalāla remains here a term of inheritance law which the text does not further define.

195.matn: ʿAbdallāh ibn Munīr narrated to us, he heard ʿAbdallāh ibn Bakr, he said: Ḥumayd narrated to us, from Anas, he said: “The prayer time came. Those who were near home went to their families, and some people remained. A basin of stone with water in it was brought to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. The basin was too small for him to spread his palm in it, yet all the people performed ablution. We said: How many were you? He said: Eighty and more.”
195.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Bathing and ablution from a basin, a cup, and wooden and stone vessels”. The basin is of stone and too small for the spread palm; yet all perform ablution. The number is “eighty and more”, with no more precise figure.

196.matn: Muḥammad ibn al-ʿAlāʾ narrated to us, he said: Abū Usāma narrated to us, from Burayd, from Abū Burda, from Abū Mūsā: “that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, called for a cup with water in it, washed his hands and his face in it, and sprayed (a little water from his mouth) into it.”
196.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter. The wording ends with the washing of hands and face in the vessel and the spraying into it. This version mentions no further instructions to those present.

197.matn: Aḥmad ibn Yūnus narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Abī Salama narrated to us, he said: ʿAmr ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, from his father, from ʿAbdallāh ibn Zayd, he said: “The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came, and we brought out water for him in a vessel (tawr) of brass. He performed ablution: he washed his face three times and his arms twice each, wiped his head, bringing it forward and back, and washed his feet.”
197.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter. The vessel is of brass. The numbers are: face three times, arms twice each, without mention of the elbows; wiping the head forward and back; the feet with no number. This version does not mention washing the hands at the start.

198.matn: Abū al-Yamān narrated to us, he said: Shuʿayb informed us, from al-Zuhrī, he said: ʿUbaydallāh ibn ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿUtba informed me: that ʿĀʾisha said: “When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, became heavy with illness and his pain grew severe, he asked his wives for permission to be nursed in my house, and they gave him permission. So the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went out between two men, his feet dragging on the ground, between ʿAbbās and another man.” ʿUbaydallāh said: I informed ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿAbbās, and he said: Do you know who the other man was? I said: No. He said: He is ʿAlī. And ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, used to narrate: that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said after he had entered his house and his pain had grown severe: Pour over me from seven waterskins whose ties have not been undone, so that I may perhaps leave an instruction for the people. I sat him in a washbasin (mikhḍab) belonging to Ḥafṣa, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Then we began pouring those over him until he began to signal to us: that you have done it. Then he went out to the people.
198.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Bathing and ablution from a basin, a cup, and wooden and stone vessels.” ʿĀʾisha reports the severe illness and the nursing in her house; the Prophet goes out between ʿAbbās and another man, his feet dragging on the ground. That the other man was ʿAlī is in the words of Ibn ʿAbbās to ʿUbaydallāh, not in ʿĀʾisha’s wording. After entering, he asks that water from seven still-sealed waterskins be poured over him, and he is seated in Ḥafṣa’s washbasin (mikhḍab). Then he goes out to the people. This version does not mention further circumstances or legal rulings.

199.matn: Khālid ibn Makhlad narrated to us, he said: Sulaimān narrated to us, he said: ʿAmr ibn Yaḥyā narrated to me, from his father, he said: “My uncle used to perform ablution a great deal. He said to ʿAbdallāh ibn Zayd: Tell me how you saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, perform ablution. He called for a vessel (tawr) of water, poured it over his hands and washed them three times, then put his hand into the vessel, rinsed his mouth and blew out of his nose three times from a single handful, then put his hand in, scooped with it and washed his face three times, then washed his arms up to the elbows twice each, then took water in his hand and wiped his head, taking it back and then forward, then washed his feet and said: This is how I saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, perform ablution.”
199.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Ablution from a vessel (tawr).” Rinsing the mouth and blowing the nose are done three times from a single handful. The arms are washed up to the elbows twice each; the wiping of the head goes back then forward; the feet are without a number. The narrator concludes: This is how I saw the Prophet perform ablution.

200.matn: Musaddad narrated to us, he said: Ḥammād narrated to us, from Thābit, from Anas: “that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, called for a vessel of water. A wide, shallow cup (qadaḥ raḥrāḥ) was brought with a little water in it. He put his fingers in it. Anas said: I began to look at the water springing from between his fingers. Anas said: I estimated those who performed ablution at between seventy and eighty.”
200.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter. The vessel is a wide, shallow cup with little water; the water springs from between the fingers. The number is Anas’s estimate: between seventy and eighty.

201.matn: Abū Nuʿaym narrated to us, he said: Misʿar narrated to us, he said: Ibn Jabr narrated to me, he said: I heard Anas say: “The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to wash, or: he used to perform ghusl, with a ṣāʿ up to five mudd, and he performed ablution with a mudd.”
201.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Ablution with one mudd.” The uncertainty “he used to wash, or: he used to perform ghusl” is kept. The amounts are: a ṣāʿ up to five mudd for ghusl, and a mudd for ablution. The wording does not convert these into modern measures.

202.matn: Aṣbagh ibn al-Faraj al-Miṣrī narrated to us, from Ibn Wahb, he said: ʿAmr narrated to me: Abū al-Naḍr narrated to me, from Abū Salama ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿUmar, from Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: “that he wiped over the leather socks.” And that ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿUmar asked ʿUmar about that, and he said: Yes, if Saʿd narrates something to you from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, do not ask anyone else about it. Mūsā ibn ʿUqba said: Abū al-Naḍr informed me: that Abū Salama informed him: that Saʿd … and ʿUmar said to ʿAbdallāh: to the same effect.
202.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Wiping over leather socks.” The wording attests the wiping, without stating conditions or a number. ʿUmar confirms Saʿd’s report and tells Ibn ʿUmar not to ask anyone else about it. The route of Mūsā ibn ʿUqba is marked as a later scholarly note (muʿallaq) and ends with “to the same effect,” without a fully written wording.

203.matn: ʿAmr ibn Khālid al-Ḥarrānī narrated to us, he said: al-Layth narrated to us, from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, from Saʿd ibn Ibrāhīm, from Nāfiʿ ibn Jubayr, from ʿUrwa ibn al-Mughīra, from his father al-Mughīra ibn Shuʿba, from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: “that he went out for his need, and al-Mughīra followed him with a vessel (idāwa) containing water. He poured over him when he had finished his need. Then he performed ablution and wiped over the leather socks.”
203.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter. Al-Mughīra follows with a water vessel, pours over him after the need, and the Prophet performs ablution and wipes over the leather socks. This version does not state further conditions for the wiping.

204.matn: Abū Nuʿaym narrated to us, he said: Shaybān narrated to us, from Yaḥyā, from Abū Salama, from Jaʿfar ibn ʿAmr ibn Umayya al-Ḍamrī: that his father informed him: “that he saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, wipe over the leather socks.” Ḥarb ibn Shaddād and Abān followed him (in the narration) from Yaḥyā.
204.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Wiping over leather socks.” Jaʿfar’s father sees the wiping over the leather socks, without further conditions or a number. The follow-up of Ḥarb ibn Shaddād and Abān from Yaḥyā is marked as a supporting route (mutābaʿa), without a fully written wording.

205.matn: ʿAbdān narrated to us, he said: ʿAbdallāh informed us, he said: al-Awzāʿī informed us, from Yaḥyā, from Abū Salama, from Jaʿfar ibn ʿAmr, from his father, he said: “I saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, wipe over his turban (ʿimāma) and his leather socks.” Maʿmar followed him (in the narration), from Yaḥyā, from Abū Salama, from ʿAmr, he said: I saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.
205.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter. This version mentions, besides the leather socks, wiping over the turban. Maʿmar’s supporting route runs from Yaḥyā through Abū Salama to ʿAmr, without Jaʿfar, and the written wording is limited to: I saw the Prophet. Further details of the wiping are not stated there.

206.matn: Abū Nuʿaym narrated to us, he said: Zakariyyāʾ narrated to us, from ʿĀmir, from ʿUrwa ibn al-Mughīra, from his father, he said: “I was with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, on a journey. I stooped to pull off his leather socks, and he said: Leave them, for I put my feet into them while they were pure. Then he wiped over them.”
206.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “When he put his feet in while they were pure.” The Prophet stops al-Mughīra from pulling them off and gives as the reason for wiping that he had put his feet in while they were pure. What “pure” covers in detail, and what further conditions apply, this version does not decide.

207.matn: ʿAbdallāh ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, he said: Mālik informed us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār, from ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿAbbās: “that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, ate a sheep’s shoulder, then prayed and did not renew ablution.”
207.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “One who did not renew ablution after mutton and sawīq.” The wording mentions eating a sheep’s shoulder, then the prayer without renewed ablution. This version does not mention other foods or rinsing the mouth.

208.matn: Yaḥyā ibn Bukayr narrated to us, he said: al-Layth narrated to us, from ʿUqayl, from Ibn Shihāb, he said: Jaʿfar ibn ʿAmr ibn Umayya informed me: that his father informed him: “that he saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, cutting from a sheep’s shoulder. He was called to prayer, so he put down the knife, prayed, and did not renew ablution.”
208.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter. The Messenger of Allah cuts from the shoulder, is called to prayer, puts down the knife, and prays without renewed ablution. This version does not mention rinsing the mouth.

209.matn: ʿAbdallāh ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, he said: Mālik informed us, from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, from Bushayr ibn Yasār, the mawlā of Banū Ḥāritha: that Suwayd ibn al-Nuʿmān informed him: “that he went out with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in the year of Khaybar, until when they were at al-Ṣahbāʾ, which is the nearest part of Khaybar. He prayed the ʿAṣr, then called for the provisions, and nothing was brought except sawīq. He gave an order concerning it, and it was moistened. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, ate, and we ate. Then he rose for Maghrib, rinsed his mouth, and we rinsed our mouths, then he prayed and did not renew ablution.”
209.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “One who rinsed his mouth after sawīq without renewing ablution.” The place and time are al-Ṣahbāʾ, the nearest part of Khaybar, in the year of Khaybar. After ʿAṣr only sawīq is brought and moistened; after eating, before Maghrib, comes the rinsing of the mouth, without renewed ablution. The wording does not define sawīq more closely.

210.matn: And Aṣbagh narrated to us, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: ʿAmr informed me, from Bukayr, from Kurayb, from Maymūna: “that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, ate a shoulder at her home, then prayed and did not renew ablution.”
210.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “One who rinsed his mouth after sawīq without renewing ablution.” The wording mentions eating a shoulder at Maymūna’s and the prayer afterwards without renewed ablution. This version does not mention sawīq or rinsing the mouth.

211.matn: Yaḥyā ibn Bukayr and Qutayba narrated to us, both said: al-Layth narrated to us, from ʿUqayl, from Ibn Shihāb, from ʿUbaydallāh ibn ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿUtba, from Ibn ʿAbbās: “that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, drank milk, rinsed his mouth and said: It has fat (dasam).” Yūnus and Ṣāliḥ ibn Kaysān followed him (in the narration) from al-Zuhrī.
211.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Does one rinse the mouth after milk?” The Messenger of Allah rinses his mouth after drinking milk and gives the fat as the reason. Whether this is obligatory or recommended, the wording does not decide. The follow-up of Yūnus and Ṣāliḥ ibn Kaysān from al-Zuhrī is marked as a supporting route, without a fully written wording.

212.matn: ʿAbdallāh ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, he said: Mālik informed us, from Hishām, from his father, from ʿĀʾisha: that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “If one of you becomes drowsy while he is praying, let him lie down until the sleep leaves him. For if one of you prays while drowsy, he does not know: perhaps he will ask forgiveness and in doing so revile himself.”
212.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Ablution after sleep.” The wording concerns becoming drowsy in the prayer and lying down until the sleep leaves, lest one ask forgiveness and revile oneself. This version does not mention ablution or distinguish light from deep sleep.

213.matn: Abū Maʿmar narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Wārith narrated to us: Ayyūb narrated to us, from Abū Qilāba, from Anas, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, he said: “If one of you becomes drowsy in the prayer, let him sleep until he knows what he is reciting.”
213.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter. This shorter version limits the reason to knowing what one is reciting. It does not mention ablution.

214.matn: Muḥammad ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, he said: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn ʿĀmir, he said: I heard Anas (change of chain). He said: And Musaddad narrated to us, he said: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Sufyān, he said: ʿAmr ibn ʿĀmir narrated to me, from Anas, he said: “The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to perform ablution for every prayer. I said: What did you use to do? He said: The ablution would suffice one of us so long as he had not broken it.”
214.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Ablution without having broken it.” The Prophet performs ablution for every prayer; the Companions let one ablution suffice so long as it has not been broken. Whether the Prophet’s practice was an obligation or a habit, this version does not decide.

215.matn: Khālid ibn Makhlad narrated to us, he said: Sulaimān narrated to us, he said: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated to me, he said: Bushayr ibn Yasār informed me, he said: Suwayd ibn al-Nuʿmān informed me, he said: “We went out with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in the year of Khaybar, until when we were at al-Ṣahbāʾ. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed the ʿAṣr for us. When he had prayed, he called for the foods, and nothing was brought except sawīq. We ate and drank. Then the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, rose for Maghrib, rinsed his mouth, then prayed the Maghrib for us and did not renew ablution.”
215.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter. The place and time are al-Ṣahbāʾ in the year of Khaybar. After ʿAṣr only sawīq is brought; they eat and drink, and before Maghrib he rinses his mouth, without renewing ablution. This version does not mention moistening the sawīq or the others rinsing with him.
